remeasurement_note: The device was re-attached on 2026-08-29 and IMG_VERSION was still 3.27.3.0. Claims carrying "measured": "2026-08-29" are new in that pass; everything else is from 2026-08-28 and was not re-run. One 2026-08-28 claim was REFUTED by the second pass -- see refuted[0], the .rmdoc archive shape -- because the original measurement sampled a notebook, the one document class that cannot exhibit the counterexample. 2026-08-29: POST /upload was probed live for the first time, with Laith's explicit authorisation, after reMarkable's own developer documentation (https://developer.remarkable.com/documentation/xochitl) was found to state "Xochitl must not run when manually accessing document files". That makes POST /upload the only write route on this firmware that goes *through* xochitl rather than around it, and therefore the only one whose result is visible to the user without stopping or restarting the application. The probe used throwaway documents and mapped the contract in four requests. claims[14] and claims[15] are rewritten from measurement; the protocol note below is corrected.
method: GET and HEAD only. Every request was correlated against GET /log.txt, which returns the live systemd journal containing the Qt server's own rm.usb.web verdict for each request. Sentinel paths (/RMSPEC-PROBE-START etc.) were requested before and after each probe batch so the log slice could be bracketed exactly. POST /upload was probed on 2026-08-29 (see claims[14]); before that date it had never been requested in any form, including GET, because the server ignores the request method and a GET to that path could not be proven non-mutating.

claims.shape: One TCP listener bound to the single address 10.11.99.1:80 (not 0.0.0.0), owned by PID 416 = xochitl. There is no separate systemd unit for the web server.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'grep " 0A " /proc/net/tcp' -> "   1: 01630B0A:0050 00000000:0000 0A ... 3880 1 ..." (LE 01630B0A = 10.11.99.1, 0x0050 = 80, inode 3880); $ ssh remarkable 'systemctl show xochitl.service -p MainPID' -> "MainPID=416"; socket-owner scan over /proc/*/fd matched socket:[3880] to pid=416 comm=xochitl.
claims.consequence: Unreachable over Wi-Fi even when SSH-over-Wi-Fi is armed. The only lever over the HTTP API is xochitl.service itself; there is no web unit to restart.

claims.shape: 10.11.99.1/27 is bound to usb1 (CDC ECM) alone. usb0 (RNDIS) is NO-CARRIER with no IP address.
claims.evidence: $ ssh remarkable 'ip -o addr show dev usb0; ip -o addr show dev usb1' -> usb0 produced no output; "4: usb1    inet 10.11.99.1/27 brd 10.11.99.31 scope global usb1"; $ ssh remarkable 'for d in /sys/class/net/*; do printf "%s=" "$(basename $d)"; cat $d/ifindex; done' -> "lo=1 / usb0=3 / usb1=4 / wlan0=8".
claims.consequence: A client that binds or routes via usb0 will never reach the web server.

claims.shape: GET and HEAD both work. The server does not dispatch on method: the path alone selects the handler. HEAD returns identical status and Content-Type -- and, corrected 2026-08-30, it does NOT return a zero-length body: the handler writes the full body because it never learned the method was HEAD.
claims.evidence: $ curl -sS -I -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type} %{size_download}' -> "HEAD /documents/      -> 200 application/json; charset=ISO-8859-1 0"; "HEAD /log.txt         -> 200 text/plain 0"; "HEAD /assets/index.css -> 200 text/css 0". Corrected 2026-08-30 with httpx rather than curl, because curl reads and discards the body while httpx follows RFC 9110 and refuses to read one for HEAD, which is what makes the difference observable: $ httpx HEAD /documents/ -> 200, headers {content-type, transfer-encoding: chunked}, NO content-length, response.content == b''. The zero size_download curl reported was curl discarding a body, not the device omitting one.
claims.consequence: HEAD is still the safe probe for existence and content type, but it is only safe on a connection that is not reused. Because method is ignored, a POST/PUT/DELETE to a read route is indistinguishable from a GET, and a GET to a write route is indistinguishable from a POST.
claims.keepalive_hazard: A HEAD PERMANENTLY POISONS THE CONNECTION IT WAS SENT ON. The firmware writes a chunked body; a spec-conforming client reads none of it for a HEAD; the bytes stay in the socket; and the next response read on that connection begins at the chunk-size line. httpx reports `RemoteProtocolError: illegal status line: bytearray(b'105d')` -- 0x105d is 4189, the exact byte length of the listing it never consumed. Reproduced three ways on one client: HEAD then GET fails on the GET; HEAD then HEAD fails on the second; HEAD carrying `Connection: close` succeeds four times in a row with a 4189-byte GET between each. Sending `Connection: close` also changes the framing the firmware chooses -- the response then carries `connection: close` and NO `transfer-encoding`, so there is no chunked body left behind and the connection is torn down regardless. This was latent for weeks in this project: whether the poisoned connection is the one the next request picks up depends on pool timing, so the hardware probe passed until it failed two runs in three. `UsbWebApi.head` now sends the header, and only for HEAD, so GET and POST keep their connection reuse.

claims.shape: Responses are HTTP/1.1 with Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Successful /download responses send BOTH Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked in the same response. All JSON bodies are labelled "application/json; charset=ISO-8859-1" even though the payload contains UTF-8 document titles.
claims.evidence: $ curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null 'http://10.11.99.1/download/40fa3080-af19-4fa9-9a42-a73f6fb7b22d/pdf' -> "HTTP/1.1 200 / Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"Quick sheets.pdf\" / Content-Length: 6021585 / Content-Type: application/pdf / Transfer-Encoding: chunked"; $ curl -sS -D - http://10.11.99.1/documents/ -> "HTTP/1.1 200 / Content-Type: application/json; charset=ISO-8859-1 / Transfer-Encoding: chunked".
claims.consequence: Clients must not trust the advertised charset. Strict HTTP/1.1 clients that reject simultaneous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding will fail on /download.

claims.response_shape: JSON array of entry objects. DocumentType keys: Bookmarked (bool), CurrentPage (int), ID (uuid), ModifiedClient (ISO-8601 with Z), Parent (uuid or ""), Type ("DocumentType"), VisibleName (string), VissibleName (string, sic -- misspelled duplicate of VisibleName), fileType ("pdf" | "notebook"). CollectionType entries omit CurrentPage and fileType and carry Type="CollectionType".
claims.evidence:
$ curl -sS -w 'http=%{http_code} type=%{content_type} bytes=%{size_download}' http://10.11.99.1/documents/ -> "http=200 type=application/json; charset=ISO-8859-1 bytes=2902"; body begins "[
    {
        "Bookmarked": false,
        "CurrentPage": 134,
        "ID": "d3b38661-8f31-4412-a6f7-16343cc5e48c",
        "ModifiedClient": "2026-03-09T20:06:11.193Z",
        "Parent": "",

Both VisibleName and VissibleName are always present and always equal in the 9+22 entries observed; a parser should read VisibleName and treat VissibleName as a legacy alias.

claims.response_shape: Same array-of-entries shape as /documents/. The argument is a PARENT (folder) id, not a document id: entries returned all carry Parent == {parentId}.
claims.evidence: $ curl -sS 'http://10.11.99.1/documents/3807c887-677a-4ef5-b8e1-18127c716ef2' -> http=200, 8331 bytes, 22 entries, every one "\"Parent\": \"3807c887-677a-4ef5-b8e1-18127c716ef2\"" (the "Work" CollectionType); $ curl -sS 'http://10.11.99.1/documents/40fa3080-af19-4fa9-9a42-a73f6fb7b22d' -> http=200, 2902 bytes, byte-identical to the root listing (cmp -s reported IDENTICAL); $ curl -sS 'http://10.11.99.1/documents/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' -> http=200, 2902 bytes, also byte-identical to the root listing.
claims.notes: Resolution rule, measured: if {parentId} names a CollectionType, its children are returned correctly; if it names a DocumentType or does not exist, the handler silently falls back to the ROOT listing with status 200 and no error. So a 200 is not proof the id was recognised -- a client must compare the returned entries' Parent field against the id it asked for. No rm.usb.web line is logged for any of these three cases, so the oracle cannot distinguish them either.

claims.corroboration: The shipped web UI bundle constructs this URL with format as a defaulted parameter: $ ssh remarkable 'grep -o -E ".{160}/download/.{200}" /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets/index.js' -> "Tx=async(e,t=\"pdf\")=>{ ... fetch(`/download/${e}/${t}`,{method:\"get\",credentials:\"same-origin\",signal:AbortSignal.timeout(3e4)}) ... if(n.status!==200)throw new Error(`File download failed (${n.status})`)".
claims.notes: The rmdoc format is the whole reason this route matters to a client: it is a server-side archive of the document's authoritative on-disk files, and it is the only HTTP route that returns .rm stroke data.

claims.shape: ZIP archive of the document's authoritative on-disk files. Members are: <docUUID>.metadata (always), <docUUID>.content (always), <docUUID>/<pageUUID>.rm (one per page in the content's page list, INCLUDING zero-byte placeholders), and -- for a document whose fileType is not "notebook" -- <docUUID>.<fileType>, the ORIGINAL underlay. Never .local, never .pagedata, never .thumbnails, never .failure. No nesting below <docUUID>/.
claims.evidence: NOTEBOOK case (2026-08-28): $ curl -sS -o q.rmdoc 'http://10.11.99.1/download/40fa3080-af19-4fa9-9a42-a73f6fb7b22d/rmdoc' && unzip -l q.rmdoc -> "275 ... 40fa3080-af19-4fa9-9a42-a73f6fb7b22d.metadata / 16162 ... .content / 107441 ... 40fa3080-.../8cfa9c18-....rm / ... / 10553946  25 files"; $ unzip -Z1 q.rmdoc | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c -> "23 rm / 1 metadata / 1 content". PDF case (2026-08-29), on 919809bb-58fd-45df-83e1-a3404415985f, a 1-page fileType=pdf document, downloaded to host scratch, listed, and deleted in the same command: $ curl -sS -o probe.rmdoc 'http://10.11.99.1/download/919809bb-58fd-45df-83e1-a3404415985f/rmdoc' -> "bytes=8557 magic=504b0304"; $ unzip -l probe.rmdoc -> ".metadata 381 / .content 2329 / .pdf 5481 / .rm 0 (depth 1) / .rm 6051 (depth 1)"; $ unzip -Z1 probe.rmdoc | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c -> "1 content / 1 metadata / 1 pdf / 2 rm".
claims.content_member_shape: $ unzip -p probe.rmdoc '*.content' -> 22 top-level keys: cPages, coverPageNumber, customZoomCenterX, customZoomCenterY, customZoomOrientation, customZoomPageHeight, customZoomPageWidth, customZoomScale, documentMetadata, extraMetadata, fileType, fontName, formatVersion, lineHeight, orientation, pageCount, pageTags, sizeInBytes, tags, textAlignment, textScale, zoomMode. cPages present, flat top-level "pages" ABSENT, fileType "pdf", formatVersion 2, pageCount 1. So the archived .content carries the modern cPages page order and its per-page template envelope, which is the only authoritative template source (see filesystem.json file-type:.pagedata).
claims.corroboration: HEAD alone, no body transferred: $ curl -sS -I 'http://10.11.99.1/download/<id>/rmdoc' -> 919809bb Content-Length 8557; 31ec7d01 Content-Length 65178; d3b38661 Content-Length 380708, all Content-Type application/zip. d3b38661's rmdoc is 380708 bytes against the 2158068-byte device-rendered PDF that /download/{id}/pdf returns for the same document -- consistent with the archive carrying the original underlay rather than a re-render.
claims.notes: For the notebook the 23 .rm members match the 23 .rm files in the on-disk <docUUID>/ directory and the 23 PNGs in <docUUID>.thumbnails/. The server re-times the .metadata and .content members to the moment of the request while preserving original mtimes on the .rm members. CONSEQUENCE: this route is sufficient to reconstruct a complete document source -- page order, per-page template, scene bytes, and underlay -- over USB with no SSH credential. The zero-byte .rm placeholder is carried verbatim, so the three page-states rule (absent / zero-byte / v6 scene) applies to the archive exactly as it applies on disk. UNMEASURED: the epub case, because this device holds no epub document; the member is presumed to be <docUUID>.epub by symmetry and must not be asserted.

claims.shape: The USB web API does not expose the trash in any form. A trashed document is ABSENT from every listing rather than being reported with a trash-shaped Parent: no entry in any listing, at any depth, carries Parent == "trash".
claims.evidence: A full BFS over /documents/ and /documents/{parentId} reached 41 entities: 36 DocumentType + 5 CollectionType (fileType census: 23 notebook, 13 pdf, 5 absent-on-CollectionType). The on-disk census over the same store is 42: 37 DocumentType + 5 CollectionType. $ ssh remarkable 'cd $D; for f in *.metadata; do ... extract type/parent/deleted ...; done' -> "parent value census: 32 UUID / 9 empty-string / 1 trash" and "deleted flag census: 28 absent / 14 false" (never true). The set difference on-disk-minus-USB is exactly one entity, 2cf3200e-56c8-4968-a380-81756d0a44b2, whose .metadata carries "parent": "trash" and "deleted": false. The reverse difference is empty.
claims.consequence: A USB DeviceCatalog reports trashed=False on every entry it returns and that is ACCURATE, because a trashed entry is never returned. Code in a USB adapter that translates a Parent == "trash" sentinel is unreachable. The sentinel is real on disk, so an SSH or mirror adapter does need it. Note also that "deleted" is not the trash signal on this firmware -- it is absent on 28 of 42 and false on 14, never true -- and that a trashed entry's original parent is NOT preserved: the parent field's value IS "trash", so the real parent is unrecoverable and must be reported as None rather than guessed.
claims.notes: This also means the USB catalog is not a complete view of the store, and the shortfall is exactly the trash. A .failure document, by contrast, IS visible over USB: 13 pdf entries are reachable and 13 .pdf files exist on disk, 12 of which carry .failure. So .failure blocks cloud sync only (see filesystem.json file-type:.failure), not the USB catalog.

claims.shape: Folder nesting reaches depth 2 on this store, so a recursive walk is load-bearing rather than a formality: 9 entries at the root, 30 at depth 1, 2 at depth 2. A single GET /documents/ sees 9 of 41.
claims.evidence: BFS depth histogram over the walk described in route:GET /documents/ trash filtering -> "{0: 9, 1: 30, 2: 2}", max depth 2. Every CollectionType id resolved correctly: zero fallback-to-root events and zero entries whose Parent disagreed with the id requested, across all 5 folders. The silent-fallback behaviour reproduced exactly for the two non-folder cases probed in the same pass: a DocumentType id and 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 each returned the byte-identical 9-entry root listing.
claims.consequence: The walk terminates only if a visited set is kept -- the root listing is returned for any unrecognised id, so a walker that does not compare each child's Parent against the id it asked for, and does not deduplicate by ID, re-enqueues the root's folders forever.

The shipped web UI never calls this route: $ ssh remarkable 'grep -o -E "/(documents|download|upload|thumbnail|log)[a-zA-Z0-9_./{}$?=&-]*" /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets/index.js | sort | uniq -c' returned /documents/ x2, /upload, /log.txt, /download/ and no /thumbnail. It exists only for external clients.

claims.response_shape: The persistent systemd journal, rendered at microsecond precision (equivalent to journalctl -o short-iso-precise), spanning all retained boots. ~9.7 MB / ~78,500 lines at measurement time. Served with Content-Disposition: attachment and a request-time filename.
claims.evidence: $ curl -sS -D h_log.txt -o /dev/null -w 'http=%{http_code} type=%{content_type} bytes=%{size_download}' http://10.11.99.1/log.txt -> "http=200 type=text/plain bytes=9703824"; headers -> "HTTP/1.1 200 / Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"log-2026-08-28T22:56:27.txt\" / Content-Type: text/plain / Transfer-Encoding: chunked".
claims.notes: This is the oracle. See claim oracle:verdict-pairs. The journal is byte-capped, not boot-capped: $ ssh remarkable 'grep -v "^#" /etc/systemd/journald.conf | grep -v "^$"' -> "[Journal] / SystemMaxUse=50M / SystemKeepFree=20M"; $ ssh remarkable 'journalctl --disk-usage' -> "Archived and active journals take up 47.5M in the file system." So the window is already at its cap and the oldest boots rotate out continuously. Any line count, byte size, boot count, or per-category line count read from /log.txt is a property of the rolling window at the moment of the fetch, NOT a firmware constant.

claims.evidence: $ curl -sS -D h_root.txt -o b_root.html -w 'http=%{http_code} type=%{content_type} bytes=%{size_download}' http://10.11.99.1/ -> "http=200 type=text/html bytes=444"; $ curl -sS 'http://10.11.99.1/index.html' -> "200 text/html 444".

claims.shape: Multipart upload. Exactly one part, field name `file`. Returns 201 {"status":"Upload successful"} on success and 400 {"error":"No file sent"} when no part named `file` is present. The imported document is visible in GET /documents/ IMMEDIATELY, with no restart and no stop of xochitl -- xochitl performs the import itself and writes every sidecar. This is the only write path on this firmware with that property, which is what makes it the supported route for an agent writing to a tablet a human is holding.
claims.evidence: The client shape was read out of the device's own SPA bundle rather than guessed: $ ssh remarkable 'grep -o -E ".{600}/upload.{300}" /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets/index.js' -> "Cx=async(e,t)=>{try{await jd(t);const n=new FormData;n.append(\"file\",e);const r=await Pp(\"api\",()=>fetch(\"/upload\",{method:\"post\",credentials:\"same-origin\",signal:AbortSignal.timeout(3e4),body:n}));if(r.status!==201)throw new Error(`Upload failed (${r.status})`)}catch(n){throw Np(n)}}". Note the client awaits jd(t) -- GET /documents/{t} -- BEFORE uploading; that is a pre-flight refresh of the target folder view, not a parent parameter, and there is no parent parameter anywhere in the call. Four live probes then measured the contract: (a) $ curl -X POST http://10.11.99.1/upload -> 400 {"error":"No file sent"}; (b) $ curl -X POST -F 'document=@probe.pdf' .../upload -> 400 {"error":"No file sent"} (so the field name is checked, not merely the presence of a body); (c) $ curl -X POST -F 'file=@probe.pdf;type=application/pdf' .../upload -> 201 {"status":"Upload successful"}; (d) $ curl -X POST -F 'file=@testnb.rmdoc;filename=Probe Rmdoc.rmdoc;type=application/zip' .../upload -> 201 {"status":"Upload successful"}.

measured_effects.visibility: GET /documents/ went from 10 root entries to 11 immediately after probe (c), with no restart of xochitl and no reload of any kind. Contrast the SSH filesystem write path, where a page written directly to disk is invisible until xochitl re-reads the document.
measured_effects.sidecars_written_by_xochitl: For a PDF upload xochitl wrote <uuid>.metadata (266 B), <uuid>.content (718 B), <uuid>.local (34 B), <uuid>.pagedata (1 B), <uuid>.pdf (826 B, mode -rw-------), an empty <uuid>/ directory, and updated .tree. The client supplies none of these.
measured_effects.parent: The new entry carries Parent == "", i.e. root. There is no folder parameter in the route and none in the SPA's call, so an upload CANNOT target a folder -- the document always lands at the top level and must be moved afterwards by some other means.
measured_effects.visible_name_pdf: For a PDF the multipart filename sets visibleName VERBATIM, extension included: 'probe-upload.pdf' and 'Probe Named Doc.pdf' both appeared under exactly those names. A client wanting a clean title must strip the extension itself, and cannot rely on the firmware doing it.
measured_effects.visible_name_rmdoc: For a .rmdoc the ARCHIVE'S OWN .metadata visibleName wins over the multipart filename: uploading TestNb's archive under filename 'Probe Rmdoc.rmdoc' produced a document named 'TestNb'. So the two accepted container types disagree about where the title comes from, and a client must not assume the filename controls it.
measured_effects.rmdoc_accepted: .rmdoc is accepted and imported as fileType notebook, so a client can author a whole notebook -- pages, strokes, typed text -- and have xochitl import it live. Measured with a 4,252-byte archive of a real one-page notebook.
measured_effects.identity_is_not_preserved: The import RE-KEYS both identities. Uploading TestNb's own archive produced document uuid a262706d-8c89-433f-ad2b-9ec82abf102d (not 31833079-...) and page uuid 97ecf030-0911-4e4c-bc12-500bf235b8d6 (not 2302bcd7-...), while the page bytes were preserved exactly (24,534 bytes in both). So POST /upload is CREATE-ONLY: it can add a document but can never update one, and round-tripping an existing document produces a copy rather than an edit. Editing an existing page therefore still requires the SSH filesystem path, which is the path reMarkable's documentation warns against.

claims.notes: Cleanup caveat worth recording: the firmware's route table is closed at six families and none of them deletes, so a client that uploads cannot undo it over HTTP. The three throwaway documents this probe created had to be removed by hand from the tablet UI -- deleting their files over SSH while xochitl is running leaves phantom entries in the library until it reloads. Any push feature must treat 'created' as effectively irreversible from the host's point of view.

claims.shape: Every error body is a single-line JSON object {"error":"<message>"} with Content-Type application/json; charset=ISO-8859-1. FOUR status codes are in use: 200 (success, and also the silent /documents/{id} fallback), 400 (routed path, bad argument), 404 (routed path, backing file unopenable), 500 (path not routed, or backing entry unresolvable).

500: Unable to get thumbnail for entry

claims.evidence: Bodies captured verbatim: {"error":"Unknown file"} (24 bytes, status 500, from /nope-xyz, /documents, /images/, /images/foo.png, /thumbnail, /download); {"error":"Malformed URL"} (25, 400); {"error":"Filetype not supported"} (34, 400); {"error":"Can only download documents"} (39, 400); {"error":"No such entry"} (25, 400); {"error":"Missing thumbnail ID"} (32, 400); {"error":"Unable to get thumbnail for entry"} (45, 500); {"error":"Unable to open file /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets"} (66, 404).
claims.notes: Nine distinct error strings are known. "No file sent" is no longer inferred from the log oracle: it was measured on 2026-08-29 as a 400 body, returned both for a request with no multipart body at all and for one whose single part is named anything other than `file`. /upload also supplies this route table's only measured 2xx body, 201 {"status":"Upload successful"}. Status code alone is still not a sufficient discriminator -- 400 now covers six semantically different failures and 500 covers both "no such route" and "route exists, entry missing".

claims.shape: The rm.usb.web logger category in /log.txt is the server's own verdict channel. It emits exactly two line shapes: 'Bad path "<path>" "<second>"' and 'ERROR "<message>"'. A path that is NOT routed produces the PAIR (Bad path, then ERROR "Unknown file"). A path that IS routed but whose handler rejects produces a BARE ERROR line with no preceding Bad path. A path that is routed and succeeds produces NO line at all.
claims.evidence: Bracketed probe slice: $ curl http://10.11.99.1/RMSPEC-FORMAT-START ; <7 download probes> ; $ curl http://10.11.99.1/RMSPEC-FORMAT-END ; then $ curl -sS -o log5.txt http://10.11.99.1/log.txt && awk '/RMSPEC-FORMAT-START/,0' log5.txt | grep -a 'rm.usb.web' -> "Bad path \"/RMSPEC-FORMAT-START\" \"\" / ERROR \"Unknown file\" / ERROR \"Filetype not supported\" x5 / ERROR \"Can only download documents\" / ERROR \"No such entry\" / Bad path \"/RMSPEC-FORMAT-END\" \"\" / ERROR \"Unknown file\"". The two successful downloads (pdf, rmdoc) in that same batch produced ZERO lines. A separate slice confirms the same for /documents/, /documents/{id}, /thumbnail/{id} and every 200 static hit: zero rm.usb.web lines.
claims.notes: The second argument of 'Bad path' is empty in 100% of occurrences: $ grep -a 'rm.usb.web' log3.txt | grep -a 'Bad path' | sed 's/^.*rm\.usb\.web *//' | sort -u returned 59 distinct lines, every one ending in ' ""'. Practical rule for route discovery: probe a candidate, then read the log slice. Bad-path-pair = the route does not exist. Bare ERROR = the route exists and you got the arguments wrong. Silence = you got a real response.

claims.shape: The route table is closed at six path families: /documents/, /documents/{parentId}, /download/{id}/{format}, /thumbnail/{id}, /log.txt, /upload, plus the static file tree (/, /index.html, /favicon-32x32.png, /reMarkable*.woff2, /assets/<file>). Everything else is Bad path.
claims.evidence: $ grep -a 'rm.usb.web' log3.txt | grep -a 'Bad path' | sed 's/^.*rm\.usb\.web *//' | sort -u -> 59 distinct Bad path entries covering, verbatim: /about, /api, /api/, /api/v1, /battery, /bundle.js, /config, /content/{uuid}, /cover/{uuid}, /device, /deviceinfo, /document/{uuid}, /documents, /download, /export/{uuid}, /favicon.ico, /file/{uuid}, /files, /folder/{uuid}, /folders/, /health, /images/, /images/foo.png, /info, /journal.txt, /log, /logs, /main.js, /manifest.json, /metadata/{uuid}, /nope, /pagedata/{uuid}, /pages/{uuid}, /preview/{uuid}, /render/{uuid}, /robots.txt, /search, /settings, /static/<non-ascii>, /status, /storage, /thumbnail, /thumbnails/{uuid}, /trash, /v1, /version -- all followed by ERROR "Unknown file".
claims.notes: There is no versioned API prefix, no health endpoint, no device-info endpoint, no per-page or per-metadata route, and no trash/search route. Singular /document/{uuid} does not exist; only plural /documents/{parentId}. Bare /download and bare /thumbnail without a trailing slash are Bad path, while /download/ and /thumbnail/ are routed -- the trailing slash is what enters the handler.

refuted.claim: The .rmdoc archive contains exactly THREE kinds of member -- <docUUID>.metadata, <docUUID>.content and <docUUID>/<pageUUID>.rm -- and in particular NO .pdf. (This spec's own 2026-08-28 claim.)
refuted.observation: Refuted 2026-08-29. The three-member shape holds only for a NOTEBOOK, and 40fa3080-af19-4fa9-9a42-a73f6fb7b22d -- the single document the original measurement sampled -- is a notebook, the one document class that has no underlay on disk and therefore cannot exhibit the counterexample. On a fileType=pdf document the archive carries a FOURTH member, the original underlay: $ unzip -Z1 probe.rmdoc | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c -> "1 content / 1 metadata / 1 pdf / 2 rm" for 919809bb-58fd-45df-83e1-a3404415985f. The .pdf member is 5481 bytes against an 8557-byte archive. This is the same generalisation error the dbus.json refutation "a single introspect of one object does not establish a universal" already records, committed in the same session that recorded the warning.
refuted.correction: See claim artifact:.rmdoc archive shape. The archive is .metadata + .content + one .rm per page + <docUUID>.<fileType> when fileType is not notebook. The consequence is large: GET /download/{id}/rmdoc is sufficient to reconstruct a COMPLETE document source over USB -- page order and per-page template from the archived .content cPages, scene bytes from the .rm members, and the underlay from the .pdf member -- with no SSH credential. Two docstrings in rmspec-domain that asserted the USB API cannot serve scene bytes were written against the refuted claim and are wrong.

refuted.claim: The USB web API models the trash as a parent value, so an adapter translates a trash-shaped Parent into trashed=True plus the entry's real parent. (Asserted in packages/rmspec-domain/src/rmspec/domain/ports/device.py, DeviceDocument docstring.)
refuted.observation: Refuted 2026-08-29 for this transport. Over USB no entry in any listing at any depth carries Parent == "trash": a trashed document is simply absent. The BFS reaches 41 of the 42 on-disk entities and the single missing one, 2cf3200e-56c8-4968-a380-81756d0a44b2, is the only entity whose on-disk .metadata carries "parent": "trash". The second half of the claim is also wrong wherever the sentinel IS present: the parent field's value IS the string "trash", so an entry's original parent is not preserved anywhere and there is no "real parent" to report.
refuted.correction: See claim route:GET /documents/ trash filtering. Over USB, trashed is always False and that is accurate because trashed entries are never returned; sentinel-translating code in a USB adapter is unreachable. On disk the sentinel is real and a trashed entry's parent_uuid is None, which is what DocumentMetadata.parent_uuid already documents. Separately, "deleted" is not the trash signal on this firmware: absent on 28 of 42 metadata files, false on 14, never true.

refuted.claim: GET /download/{id}/{name} -- the third path segment is a filename, and the route always returns application/pdf.
refuted.observation: Neither half survives. The third segment is a FORMAT selector, not a filename: every filename-shaped value returned 400 {"error":"Filetype not supported"} -- "note", "note.pdf", "note.rmdoc", "note.zip", "note.epub", "note.rm", and the URL-encoded document title "Quick%20sheets" all failed. Only the exact lowercase strings "pdf" and "rmdoc" succeed. And the content type is not always application/pdf: format=rmdoc returns 200 with Content-Type: application/zip and a PK\x03\x04 body. The shipped web UI bundle confirms the parameter's role: `Tx=async(e,t="pdf")=>{ ... fetch(`/download/${e}/${t}`, ...)`.
refuted.correction: See claim route:GET /download/{id}/{format}. Filename is server-generated into Content-Disposition from VisibleName, not supplied by the caller.

refuted.claim: GET /documents/{id} on a DocumentType id returns the ROOT listing, not that document -- the endpoint does not validate its argument.
refuted.observation: The DocumentType half reproduces exactly (byte-identical 2902-byte root listing, cmp -s IDENTICAL), and an unknown UUID behaves the same way. But "does not validate its argument" is too strong: a CollectionType id IS resolved correctly. /documents/3807c887-677a-4ef5-b8e1-18127c716ef2 returned 8331 bytes / 22 entries, every one with Parent set to that collection id.
refuted.correction: The argument is a parent/folder id. It resolves for CollectionType and silently falls back to root for anything else. A 200 does not confirm the id was recognised; compare the returned Parent field against the requested id.

refuted.observation: It does not. $ curl -sS 'http://10.11.99.1/images/' -> 500, body {"error":"Unknown file"}, and the oracle logged "Bad path \"/images/\" \"\"" then "ERROR \"Unknown file\"". Same for /images/foo.png. There is no images directory on disk: $ ssh remarkable 'ls -A /usr/share/remarkable/webui/' -> assets, favicon-32x32.png, index.html, reMarkableSans.woff2, reMarkableSerif.woff2.
refuted.correction: The static tree is the web root's five entries plus the three files under assets/. /images/ is not a route on 3.27.3.0.

refuted.claim: Error contract: {"error": "<msg>"}. Unknown path -> 500 "Unknown file". Bad request -> 400.
refuted.observation: The body shape and those two status mappings hold, but the contract has a third and fourth code and more strings than stated. GET /assets/ returns 404 with {"error":"Unable to open file /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets"} -- a status code absent from the stated contract. GET /thumbnail/{unknown-uuid} returns 500 with {"error":"Unable to get thumbnail for entry"} -- a 500 that is NOT "Unknown file" and NOT an unknown path.
refuted.correction: Four status codes (200/400/404/500) and nine known error strings. See claim error-contract. 500 means either "path not routed" or "routed, entry unresolvable".

refuted.claim: rm.usb.web has exactly TWO message shapes and a closed 5-value ERROR vocabulary: Unknown file, Malformed URL, No file sent, Filetype not supported, Unable to open file /usr/share/remarkable/webui/assets.
refuted.observation: The two line shapes hold. The 5-value vocabulary does not: probing the thumbnail and download argument space produced four more strings this session, each logged by rm.usb.web -- "Missing thumbnail ID", "Unable to get thumbnail for entry", "Can only download documents", "No such entry".
refuted.correction: At least nine ERROR strings exist. The vocabulary is open-ended with respect to probe coverage, not closed: it grows as new argument shapes are exercised, so a spec should treat the list as a lower bound.

refuted.claim: GET /log.txt returns the live system journal (~5 MB).
refuted.observation: It is the journal, but the size is not a constant. Measured 9,703,824 bytes / ~78,500 lines this session, against a journald cap of SystemMaxUse=50M with 47.5M already in use and 6 retained boots. The window is at its cap and rotating.
refuted.correction: Treat /log.txt size, line count, retained-boot count, and every per-category line count as rolling-window observations timestamped at fetch, never as firmware facts.

refuted.observation: It is advertised as "application/json; charset=ISO-8859-1" while the body carries UTF-8 document titles.
refuted.correction: Ignore the advertised charset and decode as UTF-8.
